Welcome @rajparekh_ to the Monad Foundation team!

Raj brings exceptional product leadership in the payments and stablecoin space, and genuine passion for the crypto industry. He joins us with the goal of massively growing Payments and Stablecoins on Monad.

Raj has been putting in the work to grow adoption of blockchain since 2019, when he was the founding product manager of Visa’s crypto team.

After leading Visa’s global crypto product and helping the team there to make foundational investments in integrating crypto, Raj co-founded Portal in 2021 with David Scrobonia, Parsa Attari, and Rami Shahatit.

Their vision was to massively increase crypto adoption by enabling any company to quickly add crypto wallets to any app.

Over the past four years, the Portal team has built a super powerful SDK and MPC wallet product that makes it super easy for companies to give their users crypto wallets.

Portal’s SDKs power companies like Bitso (#1 exchange in LatAm), Velo (digital dollar accounts in Brazil), Takenos (platform for LatAm-based freelancers & contractors), Rally (social trading platform, acq by OpenSea), Slingshot (acq MagicEden), Rain Cards (leading stablecoin-backed debit card), and many more.

The Portal team's story mirrors the Monad story - building tools that change the game for adoption - just starting at a different part of the stack. Their tools and their skills are truly complementary.

I feel super blessed to get the chance to work closely with Raj and the team. There's so much to do, and we're just getting started!

On behalf of the Monad Community, welcome Raj!

tweets.text:
Almost 4 years ago, I walked away from my dream job as an AI researcher to build something of my own. It’s been incredibly rewarding but incredibly lonely. 

I’m still not sure it was the “right” decision for my personal happiness, but to anyone else considering going all in on something of their own, here’s a bit about me and why I am still going for it.

I grew up in a small, conservative town in the midwest. I was taught to work hard, be nice, and follow the rules. But I wanted to do something BIG! 

At 20 yo, I discovered AI and went all in. Wrote 6 patents and 4 papers during my time in college & big tech.

But the lack of freedom imposed by bureaucracy was too much. I had unique ideas that I wanted to bring to life, whether or not my boss would approve. 

At 25, someone told me: “You can easily raise money from investors to work on one of your own ideas. All you need is a pitch & a team.” Freedom never felt so obtainable!

So I quit my job.
Grew a team. 
Failed to raise money... 
Pivoted many times
Hit my lowest mental low EVER.
Got customers.
Successfully raised money.
Learned more in 3 years, than the prior 10.

The clearest learning: “doing your own thing” is HARD.

Having money & a community to support you is essential, but the number 1 reason I continue doing the hard thing, at the expense of a lot of my close relationships and hobbies, is  this:

I don’t see anyone else pursuing the same vision; a vision that I believe will make the lives of millions so much better.

So to someone considering whether or not to go all in, my main question to you is: 
“will your vision for the world happen without you?” 

If the answer is no, I REALLY hope you go for it! The world is more fun, and efficient, when people go for their wild ideas. 

Even just trying will bring you clarity. You’ll learn if it’s worth the cost. If it’s feasible. If it’s truly unique.

We are putting together a little incentive to help people make that first step:

Free flights, food, and housing for 3 months in a San Francisco mansion that Sam Altman visited a month ago. Money + community covered ✅

Take the gap semester, you can always go back. 
Quit your job, you can always get a new one.
If a wild idea has been lingering, maybe it’s time to find out why.

We are most excited to support respectful people who are doing cool/good things that wouldn’t exist without them. 

Filmmakers, founders, artists, researchers, fashion designers, whatever you are, if you are uniquely shooting for the stars, doing something of your own (or with a small team), checkout the link below for more info.

The world needs more people with conviction, not credentials.
